content.title: About
content.content: Acerola cherry (Malpighia emarginata), also known as Barbados cherry or West Indian cherry, is a tropical fruit-bearing shrub native to South America, Central America, and the Caribbean. Celebrated for its bright red color and sweet-sour taste, it is an extraordinarily rich botanical source of vitamin C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Acerola cherries contain roughly 50 to 100 times more vitamin C than oranges or lemons.
Despite being called a cherry, it is botanically distinct from true cherries.
The fruit ripens rapidly and perishes quickly after harvest.
Green, slightly unripe acerola fruits contain higher vitamin C concentrations than fully red ones.
Frequently used to produce natural vitamin C supplements.

items.title: Natural Immune Booster
items.content: Highly bioavailable ascorbic acid supports immune defenses and recovery.

items.title: Antioxidant Protection
items.content: Rich in carotenoids and bioflavonoids that synergy with vitamin C.

items.title: Skin Vitality
items.content: Promotes collagen synthesis for skin repair and tone.

items.title: Energy & Vitality
items.content: Helps combat fatigue and improves non-heme iron absorption.

items.title: Gastrointestinal Upset
items.content: Excessive consumption can lead to diarrhea or stomach cramps due to massive vitamin C loads.

items.title: Kidney Stone Risk
items.content: High vitamin C intake converts partially to oxalates in the body.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy fresh where grown, or as pure juice, freeze-dried powder mixed into water, beverages, and functional foods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh acerola must be consumed within 3-5 days. Powders and extracts should be kept sealed in a cool, dark pantry.
